# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Prepared by:** AI Governance Academy
**Date:** Unknown
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

---

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff, is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. Its use of AI is at the piloting stage across three use cases:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

**What makes this urgent:**

* **Internal audit finding.** In June 2026, internal audit recorded that Tamarack has no inventory of AI systems.
* **Regulatory drivers.** The EU AI Act and GDPR.
* **Stated objective.** Governance must be in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027.

**Tamarack's existing foundations:** an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system (ISMS) and an ISO 9001 quality management system (QMS). Work on ISO/IEC 42001 is intended to start next year, although the start date is not fixed.

**Constraints that shape the design:**

* Budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* Customer data must stay in the EU.
* The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A conventional consulting engagement would hand Tamarack a finished set of documents. When the consultants leave, the knowledge of how those documents were reasoned, tested and connected leaves with them. The Guided AI GRC Build works the other way. Your team builds the system with weekly expert workshops and coaching. Tamarack therefore owns, understands and can operate every artifact from the day the program closes.

This matters for Tamarack for three reasons:

1. **Your managers already run management systems.** Your CISO and Head of Quality operate certified-style ISMS and QMS processes today. The most durable AI management system (AIMS) will be one they extend themselves, not a parallel structure imposed from outside.
2. **Your team will carry the next phase.** Your ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work next year will be carried by the people who build the system now.
3. **Accountability stays with Tamarack.** Visual inspection decisions will be made on a production line where accountability must sit with named Tamarack people.

The program runs on three principles: **Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.**

The program draws on two open frameworks:

* **GRC Workbook** (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) for governance, risk and compliance structures.
* **Slow AI Kitchen** (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) for governed workflows and human oversight.

Steering checkpoints draw on **AI Governance for Boards** (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack

### Inventory priority

The inventory in Week 2 directly addresses the June 2026 audit finding. Systems enter in the following order:

1. **Customer service chatbot.** It is already deployed, processes customer personal data under GDPR and interacts directly with the public.
2. **AI visual inspection pilot.** It sits on the critical path to the Q2 2027 production decision and affects production staff and product quality.
3. **AI sales forecasting.** It is recorded as a planned system so that it enters governance before procurement or build begins.

The inventory exercise may surface further AI use, such as AI features embedded in existing software. Any such systems will be recorded as found. Whether the finding can be closed remains a determination for Tamarack's internal audit function.

### ISO/IEC 42001 references

The readiness theme column below indicates where each week's artifacts support future ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work. It is not a statement of conformity and does not promise a certification outcome.

| Week | Focus | Tamarack tailoring | Integration with ISMS and QMS | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | AIMS charter, scope and RACI across the build team; first steering | Charter aligned with existing ISMS and QMS management review and governance bodies | Context and leadership (Clauses 4 and 5) |
| W2 | AI system inventory | Chatbot, visual inspection pilot and planned forecasting entered first | Inventory built as an extension of the ISMS asset inventory, not a separate register | Scope and AI resources (Clause 4, Annex A.4) |
| W3 | Classification and risk methodology | EU AI Act classification of each inventoried system (confirm with external counsel) | ISMS risk criteria and scales adapted for AI-specific harms | Risk criteria (Clause 6.1) |
| W4 | Risk and impact assessments | Chatbot impact assessment linked to GDPR data protection assessment; visual inspection assessment covering quality, safety and workforce effects | Links to existing GDPR records and QMS risk records | AI system impact assessment (Clause 6.1.4, Annex A.5) |
| W5 | Risk register and treatment | Treatment plans for the chatbot and the inspection pilot | AI risks held in the existing risk register structure | Risk treatment (Clause 6.1.3) |
| W6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core AI policy set drafted and taken to steering for adoption | Policies issued under QMS document control | AI policy (Clause 5.2, Annex A.2) |
| W7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle gates for the move of visual inspection from pilot to production | QMS design and change control extended to AI lifecycle gates | Operation and lifecycle (Clause 8, Annex A.6 and A.7) |
| W8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection starts | Chatbot vendor review including EU data residency of customer data | ISMS supplier security process extended to AI suppliers | Third-party relationships (Annex A.10) |
| W9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | Human oversight design for chatbot escalation and inspection decisions; works council consultation completed before production staff are affected (confirm with external counsel) | QMS nonconformance handling for inspection outcomes | Use of AI systems (Annex A.9) |
| W10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Inspection performance compared with the existing inspection baseline; chatbot quality monitoring | QMS measurement and monitoring processes | Monitoring and evaluation (Clause 9.1) |
| W11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident categories added to existing response routes | ISMS incident process and QMS corrective action extended | Improvement (Clause 10) |
| W12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Internal auditors lead a readiness walkthrough of the evidence | Feeds the existing internal audit programme and management review | Internal audit and management review readiness (Clauses 9.2 and 9.3) |

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS consisting of six elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

Evidence collection starts in Week 8, which provides at least four weeks of evidence by Week 12.

**Dependency requiring a Week 1 decision.** Today, only the chatbot is in production use. Visual inspection is a pilot, and the date it enters production within Q2 2027 is Unknown. The second governed workflow in production use is therefore Unknown at proposal stage. Possible routes include:

* aligning the visual inspection go-live with the program close; or
* governing another AI use identified during the Week 2 inventory.

Steering must confirm the route in Week 1. The six-element definition does not change.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

The figures below are **estimates** of hours per person per week. They assume a live workshop of about 90 minutes, a coaching session of about 60 minutes and asynchronous work in between. Final session lengths are confirmed at mobilization. Named individuals for each role, other than the sponsor, are Unknown.

| Role | Typical weekly hours (estimate) | Peak weeks and peak hours (estimate) | Primary contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| General Counsel (Sponsor) | 3 to 4 | W1, W3, W6, W9, W12: 5 to 6 | Charter, EU AI Act and GDPR positions, policy adoption, works council coordination |
| CISO | 3 to 5 | W2, W3, W8, W11: 6 to 7 | ISMS integration, supplier security, incident response |
| Head of Quality | 4 to 6 | W6, W7, W10, W11: 7 to 8 | QMS integration, document control, lifecycle and corrective action |
| Head of Data | 4 to 6 | W2, W4, W8, W10: 7 to 8 | Inventory, data governance, model monitoring |
| German plant manager | 2 to 3 | W4, W9, W10: 5 to 6 | Visual inspection risk, human oversight on the line, works council liaison |
| Internal auditors (each of two) | 2 to 3 | W11, W12: 5 to 6 | Readiness challenge and evidence walkthrough |

**Internal audit independence.** Because internal audit raised the original finding, we recommend that both internal auditors act as readiness reviewers rather than authors of controls. This preserves their independence for future audits of the AIMS.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at three points:

* **Week 1:** approve scope, team and the second-workflow route.
* **Week 6:** review spine status, adopt the policy set and make any scope decisions.
* **Week 12:** receive the minimum viable AIMS attestation against the six-element definition and the 12-month operating plan.

Each checkpoint is prepared using the AI Governance for Boards reference.

## 7. Logistics and Price

* **Duration and cadence.** Twelve weeks, delivered virtually. Each week includes one live workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation.
* **Storage.** Program artifacts are stored in Tamarack-controlled storage within the EU, consistent with the customer data constraint.
* **Price.** US$60,000, which sits within the approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* **Payment terms.** Unknown, to be set in the engagement agreement (confirm with external counsel).
* **Start date.** Unknown. For illustration, a start in the week of 11 January 2027 would close in the week of 29 March 2027, ahead of the Q2 2027 production objective.

## 8. Next Step

We propose the following steps ahead of your decision date of 15 December 2026:

1. Confirm the decision and agree a start week.
2. Nominate a named individual for each build team role.
3. Open early contact with the German works council on the scope of the visual inspection work (confirm with external counsel).
4. Review and sign the engagement agreement (confirm with external counsel).

We will then issue the Week 1 mobilization brief.
